Given that $R$ is the type III region shown above, 
${∭}_{R}2y\,\text{d}V=$
question.worked_solution:
For a type III region $R$ with projection $D$ onto the $xz$-plane, the triple integral of a continuous function $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ is given by

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A.
$$

We consider the region $R$ as a type III region enclosed between the back surface $y={u}_{1}(x,z)=1$ and the front surface $y={u}_{2}(x,z)=2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/2f1112a1fa4e540ce8ef2d1337383a2adcb378ba519cfb9c49a4521e5bc1b02f.png)

So, the region $R$ is given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,1\le y\le 2\}.
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type II *plane* region in the $xz$-plane with the left curve

$$
x={z}^{2}.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/2dcbae12ed3351892c63117f86bab7ffe6e1818b7a16666b42c2efdcc6bd787f.png)

Hence, $D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,{z}^{2}\le x\le 1\}.$

Therefore, we write the triple integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}2y\,\text{d}V & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{1}^{2}2y\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{z}^{2}}^{1}[{\int }_{1}^{2}2y\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{z}^{2}}^{1}[{y}^{2}]_{y=1}^{y=2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{z}^{2}}^{1}3\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$
